*61.  DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO :

Karnataka from 17th to 20th August, 2003 and to Andhra Pradesh from 
3rd to 7th November, 2003 to assess the drought situation for sanctioning 
of financial assistance and foodgrains for relief employment to tackle the 
drought.

the High Level Committee (HLC), headed by the Deputy Prime Minister, 
an assistance of Rs. 115.8&crores from National Calamity Contingency 
Fund (NCCF) was released to Karnataka. The HLC is yet to consider 
the proposal in respect of Andhra Pradesh on the quantum of assistance 
from NCCF, etc. 
5. Foodgrains for relief works: In the meantime, 1.65 lakh MTs of 
foodgrains to Karnataka and 1 lakh MTs of foodgrains to Andhra Pradesh 
have been released for relief employment in the wake of drought declared 
this year.

DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: †

been found affecting children instead of helping them; 
(d) if so, whether Centre has been informed that in number of States,

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (f) A Statement is laid on the Table 
of the Sabha. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary 
Education (NP-NSPE), popularly ca lled the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, 
covers all children of primary cl asses studying in Government, 
Government-aided and Local Body Schools throughout the country. Last 
year, .the scheme was expanded to cover Education Guarantee and 
Alternate or innovative Education Centres under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan 
also. Leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha and Chief Minister of Tamil 
Nadu have suggested expansion of the scheme so as to cover children 
upto class VIII and X respectively. 
(c)'to (e) There have been newspaper  reports to the effect that 
children in some schools of Delhi took ill on certain days after consuming 
the mid-day meal. Delhi Administration has been requested to report full 
facts, and take corrective action. Government of Andhra Pradesh has 
reported that 1378 children took ill in the State during January to 
November, 2003, after consuming mid-day meal. Government of 
Karnataka has reported that there we re no such incidents in the State. 
Information from other States is being collected. 
(f) State Governments have been advised to take the following steps 
in this regard : 
(i)   ensure that food under the Mid-day Meal Programme is cooked, 
served and consumed in a hygienic manner, (ii)   involve 
Women's Self Help Groups in cooking mid-day meals, 
as far as possible, and (iii)   adopt/adapt practices followed in mid-day 
meal programme which are running well through NGOs (like ISKCON 
and Nandi Foundation). Efforts are also being made to provide financial 
support to States for meeting a part of the cooking cost from funds 
available under Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) of the 
Planning Commission.

Auxiliary Warning System in Railways 
 
*69. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of 
RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Railways is planning to adopt a new Auxiliary Warning 
System to strengthen the safety and  security of passengers and rail 
installications; 
(Jo) what is the difference between AWS and the train protection and 
warring system recommended by Khanna Committee; and 
(c) how the outside interference with rail installations such as track 
and signalling equipment is likely to be curtailed with the help of the 
above warning system? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS SHRI NITISH KUMAR: (a) Yes, Sir. 
It has been planned to adopt Train Protection and Warning System 
(TPWS), a variant of Auxiliary Warning System (AWS), to further enhance 
safety levels in train operations by preventing cases of 'Signal Passed at 
Danger' in 280 Track kilometres of 'A' route on Southern and North Central 
Railways, on trial basis. 
(b) Functionality wise there is no difference between the two systems, 
which are basically meant to prevent  driver passing signal at danger. 
However, both the system use different technologies to achieve the 
intended functionality. 
(i) The conventional AWS system uses track magnets, which are 
basically made of Copper, as track device making it prone to thefts. 
Information about signal aspect, in AWS, is transmitted from track 
device to cab equipment through electro magnetic induction. 
(ii) TPWS uses Euro Balise as a track device, which is an electronic 
device with very less Copper inside and it uses radio transmission 
for sending information to cab equipment.

(c) TPWS is basically meant to prevent driver from passing a signal 
at danger thereby preventing accid ent thereof. The system does not 
have any functionality, which can cu rtail outside interference of rail 
installations, such as track and signalling equipment.

of the Task Force on Women and Children chaired by Shri T.N. 
Chaturvedi, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) met on 16.7.2001 and 
reviewed the Dowry Prohibition Act (1961) and the amendments thereto. 
It also considered the draft model Rules prepared by the Department of 
Women and Child Development for enforcement and implementation of 
the Dowry Prohibition Act. The Department had suggested constitution

more important suggestions are encapsulated below:

the giving and taking of dowry as an offence. 
(ii) Simultaneously a social movement through awareness campaigns 
and by educating the younger generation on the evils of dowry 
should be initiated.

and taken during the wedding should be made mandatory wish 
the certification of registration.

mandatory, who should be giv en clear and defined power under 
the Act so that they can function effectively.

to the Chief Ministers of all States by the Minister of Human 
Resource Development in August, 2002 drawing their attention to 
the need to curb this social evil.

that the Government should have relook at this policy to make it people 
friendly. In its reply to the Committee the Government has informed its 
stand that the policy is balanced and rational and needs no change at 
present. 
The Government announced the 'Pharmaceutical Policy 2002' in 
February, 2002. However, a public interest litigation filed in the High Court 
of Karnataka at Bangalore resulted in an Order dated 12-11-02 which 
stopped the Government from implementing the price control regime of 
the Pharmaceutical Policy 2002. This Department filed a Special Leave 
Petition (SLP) before the Supreme Court of India against the Order of 
the Karnataka High Court, which has been admitted as SLP (C) No. 
3668/2003. The Supreme Court vide its order dated 10-3-2003 
directed the Government, interaiia, to "consider and formulate appropriate 
criteria for ensuring essential and life saving drugs not to fall out of the 
price control and further directed to review drugs, which are essential 
and life saving in nature till 2nd May, 2003". Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare has brought out the National List of Essential Medicines, 2003 
after the review of the National Essential Drugs List, 1996.

nearly 12 per cent of the total disease burden in the State of Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and Government's reaction thereto; 
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to reduce the pollution of the river

Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMEN T AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU) : (a) to.(d) According to t he draft report of the World Bank 
sponsored study en the 'State of Environment Report and Action Plan 
for Uttar Pradesh' of August, 2002 on the water quality of the river Ganga 
in the Uttar Pradesh stretch of the river, the Water Quality Index as per 
an index developed by the National Sanitation Foundation of the United 
States, was below 42 for the period 1995-2001 on a 0-100 scale. The 
study does not attribute the disease burden reported to the water quality 
of the river Ganga alone. 
Government has been aware of the pollution of the river Ganga well 
before the World Bank study was carr ied out. In order to address this 
problem, Government launched the Ganga Action Plan in 1986. Under 
the Ganga Action Plan and subsequent action plans for its tributaries, 
currently 1645 million litres per day of  sewage is being intercepted, 
diverted and treated. On completion of the on-going phase of the Ganga 
Action Plan by the year 2007, a total amount of 2381 million litres per 
day of sewage shall be intercepted, diverted and treated. As per the 
water quality monitoring reports of the Ministry carried out through 
different reputed institutions, the wa ter quality of the river Ganga has 
shown significant improvement in Dissolved Oxygen (DO) and 
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD). However, faecal coliform levels of 
the river continue to be high in relation to water quality standards for 
bathing, in the stretch from Kanpur downstream. 
The World Bank sponsored study has utilized the Water Quality Index 
developed by the National Sanitation Foundation of the United States. 
46 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
This Index is not widely accepted as it is subjective, does not provide 
use based risk and has other limitations. The study also does not report 
individual parameters used for the index in respect of which Indian water 
quality standards have been notified.

relate to water shortages and flooding, urban outdoor air pollution, indoor 
air pollution, solid waste, land degradation and forest & biodiversity loss. 
Government is addressing these problems through the enforcement of 
various statutory provisions and through programmes implemented by 
different departments.

357. SHRI S. AGNIRAJ: W ill the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The Southwest Monsoon 
rainfall during 2003 for the country as a whole was 102% of the long 
period average (LPA).

range forecast for Northeast mons oon (October—December) season.

country as a whole was 108% of the LPA.

Northeast Monsoon has brightened t he prospects of Kharif and Rabi 
crops in 2003-04. According to the first advance estimate, the Kharif 
Foodgrains production for 2003-04 is 108.45 million tonnes compared 
with 90.48 million tonnes in 2002-03 (4th advance estimate). Similarly 
Kharif Oilseeds production for 2003- 04 has been estimated at 15.08 
million tonnes compared with 9.22 million tonnes in 2002-03.

36% was surplus over their own consumption.

promotion of watershed development programmes, emphasis on 
developing and promoting new technologies, measures for increasing

Agricultural Insurance Scheme etc. Besides, the Government also 
encourage farmers to increase produ ction through price policy which 
includes implementation of Minimum Support Price and Market 
Intervention Schemes. Apart from these, the Government have also 
adopted macro-management mode for providing assistance to the States. 
The Macro-Management Scheme integrates 27 schemes into one for 
supplementing and complementing the efforts of State Governments 
through work plans. This gives flex ibility to States to address specific 
problems faced by them depending on local requirements, avoid 
overlapping in the contents of diffe rent schemes and aim at all-round 
development of agriculture. These schemes are being continued with a 
view to improving production and productivity in agriculture in different 
States/regions in the country. Besides, with a view to pass on the benefit

Effect of subsidy given by developed countries to farmers 
† 364.  SHRI LAJPAT RAI: 
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to refer to answer to 
Unstarred Question 2374, given in the Rajya Sabha on the 13th 
December, 2002 and state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the subsidy being given by America and 
other developed countries to their farmers on a large scale in agriculture 
sector is against the agreement with World Trade Organisation; 
(b) if so, whether the subsidy by these countries could not be banned 
through World Trade Organisation; and 
(c) it so, the future planning of India in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The Agreement on 
Agriculture of the World Trade Org anisation (WTO) provides the rules 
and disciplines on, inter alia, domestic support and export subsidies, in 
respect of the agricultural products or groups of products by each WTO 
Member, including the United States. Accordingly, the United States is 
not authorized by the WTO agreements to provide subsidies in excess 
of the budgetary outlays and quantity commitment levels specified in its 
Schedule in favour of its domestic producers or exporters. In case any 
WTO Member perceive that any other WTO Member has failed to 
implement the rule and disciplines of the WTO agreements or has 
exceeded the specific binding commitments limiting subsidization, that 
Member can invoke the dispute settlement mechanism of the WTO and 
legally challenge the subsidies extended by the other WTO Member. For 
instance, Brazil has challenged the subsidies extended by the United 
States to its cotton farmers, and India is participating in this dispute as 
a third party.

(c) Recognising that the Uruguay Round results on curtailing trade-
distorting domestic support and ex port subsidies would not meet the 
objective of establishing a fair, market-oriented agriculture trading system, 
and that the process of reform of trade in agriculture has to be continued, 
Article 20 of the Agreement on Agriculture provides for initiation of the 
negotiation of further commitments on support and protection from 1 
January, 2000. The Doha Ministerial Declaration of 14 November, 2001 
further elaborates that these negotiations shall aim to substantially reduce 
trade-distorting domestic support an d phase out all forms of export 
subsidies. These negotiations are scheduled to conclude by 1 January, 
2005. In order to ensure that the objectives of the Doha mandate for 
negotiations are fully met, India along with other WTO Members including 
Argentina, Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Philippines, South Africa 
and Zimbabwe, as Member of the G-20 alliance on agriculture have 
been pressing for substantial reductio ns in trade-distorting domestic 
support and time bound elimination of export subsidies by the heavy 
subsidizing developed countries such as the United States and the 
European Union.

† 365. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Go vernment are considering to enact a 
law for contract farming under pressure from various companies; 
(b) whether it is also a fact th at Government have not consulted 
farmers' organization in this regard; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
IRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) and (c) An Expert Committee having representatives of farmers, 
-up by the Ministry of Agriculture on strengthening and developing of 
agricultural marketing in its report in June, 2001 made several 
recommendations for promotion cf an alternative marketing system in 
private   and cooperative sector. The recommendations made by the 
Expert Committee were examined by an inter-Ministerial Task Force 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
72 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
constituted by this Ministry. The Ta sk Force in its report has observed 
that small farmers in India are generally capital starved and cannot make 
major investment in land improv ement and modern inputs. Contract 
farming can fill up this gap by providing the farmers with quality inputs, 
technical guidance and management skills: Although the company deals 
only with the contract crop, the farmers' overall management skill may 
improve, thereby helping them to ra ise the yields of both contract and 
non-contract crops. 
With a view of to safeguard the interests of farmers under Contract 
Farming, the Task Force has inter-alia made the following: 
recommendations:- 
(i) The contract farming should be made  legal. In case of violation of 
contract, from either side, farmers as well as the company should 
be in a position to approach an organization or institution, which 
can mediate and settle the dispute. 
(ii) The contract farming should have a provision for both forward and 
backward linkages. Unless both input suppiy and market for the 
produce are assured, small farmer s will not be in a position to 
participate in contract farming. 
(iii) There should be a contract farm ers association or cooperatives at 
the plant level which will improve their bargaining power vis-a-vis 
the company and promote equality of partnership for ensuring 
smooth functioning of any contract farming arrangement. 
The recommendations of the Task Force were discussed with the 
State Governments in the National Conference on Agricultural Marketing 
Reforms held on 27.9.2002 and later by the Standing Committee of 
State Ministers on 29.1.2003, wherein this Ministry was requested to 
formulate a Model Legislation on Agri cultural Marketing in order to 
guide the States in implementing the reforms. Accordingly, a Committee 
under the Chairmanship of Additional Secretary in the Department of 
Agriculture and Cooperation has formulated a Model Legislation on 
Agricultural Marketing inter-alia containing Model Specifications of 
Contract Farming Agreement. The Model Law has been sent to all State 
Governments/UT Administrations for their consideration as the subject 
matter fails within the purview of State Governments/UT 
Administrations.

Destruction of forest areas for developmental projects 
395. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA: Will the Minister of 
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
• (a) whether it is a fact that large forest areas had been destroyed during the 
last twenty years for various developmental projects like dams, mining 
operations and setting up of industries; 
(b) if so, the details thereof State-wise and project-wise; 
. (c) whether loss of forest areas as a result of the developmental projects 
has been compensated by matching schemes of afforestation and 
development of National Parks/Sanctuarie s during the same period and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken for the rehabilit ation of the people living in the 
forest areas displaced as result of  the developmental projects in the 
forest areas? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMEN T AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) and (b) Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 regulates the diversion of 
forest land for non-forestry purposes. Prio r to enactment of this Act in 1980, 
about 45 lakh hectare of forest land was diverted in 30 years between 1950-
1980. This unabated diversion of forest  land has been effectively checked by 
the enactment of Forest (Conserva tion) Act, 1980. The annual rate of 
diversion has come down to as low as 0.38 lakh hectare per annum. Proposal 
for diversion of forest land are considered on its merit and the need to balance 
the conservation effect with the devel opmental need of the country. Since 
1980 i.e. during last 23 years, about 8.72 la kh hectare of forest land has been 
diverted for non-forestry purposes. The State-wise and Project category-wise 
details at Statement-I and Statement-ll respectively (See below). 
98 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) While diverting forest lands for non-forestry purposes under the 
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, adequate mitigatory measures are taken 
up to compensate the loss of forest areas. Among them, compensatory 
afforestation over equivalent non-forest land or degraded forest land 
double in extent as the case may be is one of the most important 
conditions stipulated by Government. Besides this, Safety zone creation 
in case of Mining projects, Catchment Area Treatment Plan in case of 
Hydro-power and Irrigation projects etc. are also stipulated by 
Government. If an area involves a National Park/Sanctuary, the concerned 
State Government/User Agency is asked to prepare a Wildlife

compensatory afforestation over 6.88 lakh hectares, about 4.84 lakh 
hectare have been achieved by various State/UT Governments so far. 
In order to ensure 100% compliance of compensatory afforestation, 
Government have decided to constitute a Compensatory Afforestation 
Management and Planning Agency. 
(d) If a project involves displacement of people, Government ensure

by the respective State/UT Government. The State/UT Government and

imposed on the recruitment of new staff for protected areas; 
(ii) Establishment of Convention on International Trade in Endangered 
Species (CITES) Cell in India;

415. SHRI GAYA SINGH: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Article 81(e) has been inserted in education code for 
Kendriya Vidyalayas in August, 2003; 
(b) if so, the salient features thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether it has since been kept in abeyance; and if so, the reasons 
therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI 
KATHIRIA):(a) As informed by Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, a 
121 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
notification for insertion of article 81 (e) in the Education Code for the 
Kendriya.Vidyalayas was issued vide KVS O.M. No. F. 11-12/2003/KVS 
(Vig.) dated 6th August 2003. 
(b) The provisions of the Article envisage a transparent as well as 
totally insulated mechanism, for taking an un-adulterated direct feedback 
from the students, on the fact of der eliction of duty as defined by the 
Article. It also provides for corrective mechanism by giving notice and 
chance to improve to those teachers/employees who are found 
responsible for dereliction of duty after the first assessment, by the 
students. The infliction of the major penalty of removal from service is 
also provided for, after the second assessment by students upon those 
who do not improve even after being given a chance after first assessment 
by the students. Principle of natural justice is followed by giving them a 
show cause notice before inflicting penalty. Provision for appeal also 
exists within the framework of the Article. 
As per KVS, insertion of this article was necessitated because in a 
school situtation, the relationship of the student vis-a-vis the teachers 
and other employees of the school with whom he directly interacts, is an 
unequal relationship because of which the misconduct committed by 
any teaching/non-teaching employee, wherein the prime witness or the 
victim is the student, cannot be normally established by following the 
provisions of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965. In this unequal relationship 
requiring the student to come forward openly with his evidence and 
allowing the teacher/employee to cross-examine him makes the child 
susceptible to retribution by the said teacher/employee or their colleagues. 
Since the students cannot be expected to take such a risk, these 
misconducts, some of which are crucial for the normal functioning of the 
school, go unpunished leading to their further commission with impunity. 
As it was felt necessary to stop the commission of such misconducts for 
the proper functioning of the school, the procedure laid down by the 
CCS (CCA) rules, 1965 was to be di spensed with for establishing the 
misconduct. 
(c) KVS has decided to re-examine this issue.

439. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the salient points of the UGC proposal to "recast the 
vocationalisation programme at the undergraduate level under a modified 
scheme of career orientation programme" under which colleges and

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI

Grants Commission (UGC), the salient points of the vocationalisation of

market oriented, skill enhancing, add-on courses that have utility

Universities/Colleges to identify their own 'need based' Career Oriented 
Courses.

462. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Will t he Minister of RAILWAYS    
be pleased to state : 
(a) what are the improvements in the sa fety and efficiency of operation of 
railways after   creation of the five new zones; 
(b) whether there has been any improv ements in the railway earning after 
the new zones coming into effect in April 2003, and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE.MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI 
BASANAGOUDA R. PATIL): (a) With the creation of smaller administrative 
railway zones, it has been possible to achieve an all round improvement in the 
functioning of the railways due to better supervision and monitoring. During 
the period April-November, 2003, while the total number of consequential train 
accidents remained at the same level, there has been a significant 
improvement in the following areas of  safety performance of the Indian 
Railways. During the period, there were 3 train collisions as against 10 train 
collisions during the corresponding period of the previous year. Similarly, the 
accidents at manned level crossing gates  have dropped from 9 to 6 and the 
train derailments from 151 to 148.

311.29 million tonnes as compared to 290.88 tonnes during the corresponding 
period of the previous year, recording an increase of 20.41 million tonnes 
implying a growth of 7%. Similarly, the total transport output in terms of Net 
Tonne Kilometres (NTKMs) increased from 202.05 Billion NTKMs to 212.60 
Billion NTKMs, which is an increase of 10.55 Billion NTKMs, indicating an 
overall growth of 5.22%. During the cu rrent year, the punctuality performance 
of passenger carrying trains in most of the new railway zones is of the order of 
95% to 98%. 
(b) and (c)   Yes, Sir. During the period April-September' 2003, the 
overall earnings of the Railways have increased to Rs. 20,414.78 crore 
as compared to Rs. 19,825.80 crore   during the corresponding period 
\of previous year, which is an increase of Rs. 588.98 crore   during the 
first half of the current year.

*42. MISS MABEL REBELLO : Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION"be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that monopo lization of procurem ent of foodgrains 
by Central and State agencies has institutionalized inefficiency; 
(b) if so, what measures Government plan to take to re duce inefficiency 
in this sector; and 
(c) to what extent the consumer s would be benefited from these 
measures? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) Under the Government Policy 
on procurement of foodgrains, the priv ate sector is also free to procure 
foodgrains from the farmers at or above the Minimum Support Price (MSP). 
The Government announces the MSP for the farmers every crop year so as to 
ensure remunerative prices to the farmers , prevent distress sale and to have 
sufficient buffer stocks for a sound' Public Distributi on System (PDS). 
Farmers have the freedom to offer their produce to public or private agencies. 
The participation of Government agencie s in the procurement of foodgrains 
has, over the years, led to the su ccessful implementation of the MSP 
operations in the country. 
(b) To further improve efficiency in the procurement operations by 
Government agencies, a number of measures have been taken, which, inter-
alia, aim at reducing the  carrying cot of foodgrains, including the transit 
losses. 
(c) The Central Issue Price of foodgrains for BPL families has remained 
unchanged since July, 2000 and the consumers under the BPL and 
Antyodaya Anna Yojana are getting foodgrains at pre-determined subsidized 
prices only.

skilled information technology professio nals in the United States, the United 
States Congress had, through the Am erican competitiveness and Workforce 
Improvement Act of 1998, progressive ly increased the H-1B visa quota 
between U.S. fiscal years 1999 and 2003.  According to that Act, the annual 
quota was to revert from 195,000 in U.S. fiscal year 2003 to the original level

far taken no legislative measure the quot a, the annual ceiling on H-1B visas

States to restrict, and regulate condit ions for, access of foreign firms and 
professionals to the Unit ed States information technology market, including 
outsourcing of Government-funded proj ects. None of these proposals have 
become law so far.

the United States to economic factor s, such as impact on employment 
opportunities for U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

information technology industry.

'universal license'? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI 
ASHOK PRADHAN): (a) Sir, inter alia, based on the recommendations 
of Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), an addendum to New

services : 
(i) Unified Licence for Telecommunication Services permitting 
Licensee to provide all Telecommunication/Telegraph services 
covering various geographical areas using any technology;

permitting Licensee to provide Basic and/or Cellular Services

recommendations.

Telecommunications on 27.10.2003, had mentioned that the present 
system of Licensing should be replaced by Unified Licensing/Automatic 
authorization Regime and that the ob jective of the Unified Licensing/ 
authorization Regime is to be achieved in two-stage process with the 
Unified Access License Regime for Ba sic and Cellular Services in the 
first phase, to be followed up with a process to define the guidelines and 
rules for fully Unified License/Authorization Regime. The 
recommendations of TRAI have been accepted and the first phase of 
Unified Access Services License Regime for Basic and Cellular Services

Statement-I 
Steps taken by the Government to promote the Information 
Technology Sector 
1. Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG) has been 
rationalised and extended uniformly to all sectors without any 
threshold limit on payment of 5% duty. 
2. Approvals for all foreign direct investment proposals relating to 
the Information Technology sector, with the exception of 
Business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce are under the 
automatic route. 
247 
 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
3. Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) and Software 
Technology Park (STP) Schemes are implemented under the 
aegis of the Department of Information Technology, Ministry of 
Communications and Information Technology, through a single 
window mechanism of the Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee 
(IMSC). 
4. Supplies of Information Technology Agreement (ITA-1) items 
in the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) by EHTP/EOU/EPZ units 
shall be counted towards fulfillment of minimum Net Foreign 
Exchange earning as a Percentage of exports (NFEP) and the 
minimum Export Performance (EP), provided that the items 
are manufactured in the unit and attract zero rate of basic 
customs duty. Positive NFEP is required to be achieved in 5 
years instead of every year. 
5. DTA access upto 50% of the FOB value of export is permitted 
for electronics hardware units under EOU/EPZ/EHTP 
schemes and the software units under EOU/EPZ/STP 
schemes. 
6. Accelerated depreciation norms extended to computers and 
computer peripherals to all units and capital goods of IT 
hardware units under Export Oriented schemes (EOU/EPZ/ 
STP/EHTP). These shall stand dep reciated to overall limit of 
90% over a period of 3 years. 
7. Special Economic Zones are being set up to enable hassle 
free manufacturing and trading for export purposes. 
8. The Depreciation on Computers is allowed @ 60%. 
9. In the Budget 2002-03, the peak rate of cumstoms duty has 
been reduced from 35% to 30%. Customs duty has been 
reduced on stepper motors for computers/printers from 5% to 
0%, floppy diskette and unrecorded magnetic tape from 15% to 
10%, ink cartridges/ribbon assembly/ribbon gear 
assembly/ribbon gear carriage for use in printers for computers 
from 25% to 5%, 56 items of capital goods for manufacture of 
semiconductors from 5% to 0%, 24 items of capital goods 
(around 200 sub-items) for manufacture of electronic 
components from 25-35% to 15%, tools/moulds/

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
dies for electronics industry from 25% to 15% and on 46 items 
of raw materials for manufacture of electronic components 
from 25-35% to 5%. 
Customs duty on Computers and Peripherals continues to be 
@ 15% and all storage devices , integrated circuits, 
microprocessors, data display tubes and deflection 
components of colour monitors continue at 0%. The 
concessional rate of customs duty @5% for specified raw 
materials for the electronics in dustry (121 items) continues. 
Customs duty on Information Technology Agreement (ITA-1) 
items of WTO (IT and Teleco m products) continues @15%, 
parts of Telecom continue @5%, parts, components and 
accessories of mobile handsets including cellular telephones 
continue at 0%.

multiple rates to single rate of 16% and single rate of Special 
Excise Duty (SED) @ 16%, in the Budget 2001-02, and 
continues.

and Excise Duty. 
12. Second-hand capital goods upto 10 years are freely 
importable. 
13. EOU/EPZ/STP/EHTP units are eligible for Income Tax benefit 
on export profits, upto 2010, in terms of Sections 10A and 10B 
of the Income Tax Act.

Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) is available to the IT sector.

Income Tax Act covere transmission of data.

developers.

Sections 10A, 10B and 80HHE of the Income Tax Act.

CBU or in CKD/SKD condition.

242. PROF M. SANKARALINGAM: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state : 
(a) the present status of Public Distribution System; 
(b) the steps taken during the current year to streamline the PDS;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI V SREENIVASA 
PRASAD): (a) The Public Distribution System (PDS) is operated under 
the joint responsibility of the Ce ntral and State Governments. The 
Central and State Government is responsible for the procurement and 
transportation of foodgrains up to t he Principal Distribution Centres of 
the Food Corporation of India while the State Governments are 
responsible for the identification of  families living Below the Poverty 
Line, the issue of Ration Cards an d distribution of foodgrains to the 
beneficiaries through Fair Price Shops. The Central and the State 
Governments work in close coordination. 
(b) Following measures have been taken by the Government for 
strengthening the Public Distribution System in the country: 
(i) The Public Distribution System  (Control) Order, 2001 has been 
issued on 31st August, 2001 unde r Section 3 of the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 with a view to curb wilful adulteration, 
substitution, diversion, theft of stocks from the Central godown 
to Fair Price Shops and at the premises of the FPS etc. 
(ii) A Task Force has been constituted to look into the irregularities 
in the implementation of the TPDS and Antyodaya Anna Yojana 
in the identified areas. 
(iii) States/UTs have been asked to actively involve the Gram 
Panchayats in rural areas and local bodies in urban areas in 
the monitoring of Fair Price Shop as a measure of social audit. 
(iv) A model Citizen's Charter has been issued to all the States./ 
UTs for adoption.

not envisage meeting the full requirements of foodgrains of any person

Area, which includes a Free Trade Area in goods, services and

countries by December 2016 and by India by December 2011.

concluded by 2007.

(EHP) on trade in goods under which progressive tariff reduction on 105 
agreed items shall commence from November 2004. Tariff elimination/ 
reduction shall be completed by Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, 
Singapore, Thailand and India by October 2007, and by Cambodia, Laos,

Adopted by the Security Council at its 4844th meeting, on 16 
October 2003 
The Security Council, 
Reaffirming its previous resolutions on Iraq, including resolution 
1483(2003) of 22 May 2003 and 1500 (2003) of 14 August 2003, and 
on threats to peace and security caused by terrorist acts, including 
resolution 1373 (2001) of 28 September 2001, and other relevant 
resolutions, 
Underscoring that the sovereignty of Ir aq resides in the State of 
Iraq, reaffirming the right of the Iraqi people freely to determine their 
own political future and contro l their own natural resources, reiterating 
its resolve that the day when Iraqi s govern themselves must come 
quickly, and recognisingihe importance of international support, 
particularly that of countries in the region, Iraq's neighbours, and 
regional organizations, in taking forward this process expeditiously, 
Recognizing that International support for restoration of conditions 
of stability and security is essentia l to the well-being of the people of 
Iraq as well as to the ability of all concerned to carry out their work on 
behalf of the people of Iraq, and welcoming Member State 
contributions in this regard under resolution 1483 (2003), 
Welcoming the decision of the Governing Council of Iraq  to  form 
a preparatory constitutional committee to prepare for a constitutional 
conference that will draft a constitu tion to embody the aspirations of 
the Iraqi people, and urging it to complete this process quickly. 
306 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
Affirming that the terrorist bombings of  the Embassy of Jordan on 
7 August 2003, of the United Nationa headquarters in Baghdad on 19 
August 2003, of the Imam Ali Mosque in Najaf on 29 August 2003, and 
of the Embassy of Turkey on 14 October 2003, and the murder of a 
Spanish diplomat on 9 October 2003 are attacks on the people of Iraq, 
the United Nations, and the international community, and deploring the 
assassination of Dr. Akila al-Has hmi, who died on 25 September 
2003, as an attack directed against the future of Iraq, 
In that context, recalling and reaffirming the statement of its 
President of 20 August 2003 (S/P RST/2003/13) and resolution 1502 
(2003) of 26 August 2003, 
Determining that the situation in Iraq, although improved, 
continues to constitute a threat to international peace and security, 
Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of United Nations, 
1. Reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq, and 
underscores, in that context, the temporary nature of the 
exercise by Coalition Provisional  Authority (Authority) of the 
specific responsibilities, aut horities, and obligations under 
applicable international law recognized and set forth in 
resolution 1483 (2003), which will cease when an 
internationally recognized, representative government 
established by the people of Iraq is sworn in and assumes the 
responsibilities of  the Authority, inter-alia through steps 
envisaged in paragraphs 4 through 7 and 10 below; 
2. Welcomes the positive response of the international 
community, in for a such as the Arab League, the Organization 
of the Islamic Conference, the United Nations General 
Assembly, and the United Nation s Educational, Scientific and 
Cultural organization, to the establishment of the broadly 
representative Governing Council as an important step towards 
an internationally recognized, representative government; 
3. Supports the Governing Council's efforts to mobilize the people 
of Iraq, including by the appointme nt of cabinet of ministers and 
a preparatory constitutional committee to lead a process in which 
the Iraqi people will progressively  take control of their own 
affairs. 
307 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
4. Determines that the Governing Council and its ministers are 
the principal bodies of the Iraqi interim administration, which, 
without predjudice to its fu rther evolution, embodies the 
sovereignty of the State of Iraq during the transitional period 
until an internationally recogn ized, representative government 
is established and assumes the responsibilities of the Authority; 
5. Affirms that the administration of Iraq will be progressively 
 undertaken by the evolving structures of the Iraqi interim 
administration. 
6. Calls upon the Authority, in this context, to return governing 
responsibilities and authorities to the people of Iraq as soon as 
practicable and requests the Authority, in cooperation as 
appropriate with the Governing Council and the secretary-
General, to report to the Council on the progress being made; 
7. Invites the Governing Council to provide to the Security Council, 
for its review, no later than 15 December 2003, in cooperation with 
the Authority and, as circumstances permit, the Special 
representative of the Secretary-General, a time-table and a 
programme for the drafting of a new consitution for Iraq and for the 
the holding of democratic elections under that constitution; 
8. Resolves that the United Nations, acting through the Secretary-
General, his Special Representative, and the United Nations 
Assistance Mission in Iraq, should strengthen its vital role in Iraq, 
including by providing humanitarian relief, promoting the economic 
reconstruction of and conditions for sustainable development in 
Iraq, and advancing efforts to restore and establish national and 
local institutions for representative government; 
9. Requests that, as circumstances permit, the Secretary-General 
pursue the course of action outlined in paragraphs 98 and 99 of 
the report of the Secretary-General of 17 July 2003 (S/2003/715); 
10. Takes note of the intention of the Governing Council to hold a 
constitutional conference and, reco gnizing that the convening of 
the conference will be a milestone in the movement to the full 
exercise of sovereignty, ca//s for its preparation through national 
dialogue and consensus-building as soon as practicable and 
requests the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, 
308 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
at the time of the convening of the conference or, as 
circumstances permit, to lend the unique expertise of the United 
Nations to the Iraqi people in this process of political transition, 
including the establishment of electoral processes; 
11. Requests the Secretary-General to ens ure that the resources of 
the United Nations and associated or ganizations are available, if 
requested by the Iraqi Governing Council and, as circumstances 
permit, to assist in furtherance of  the programme; provided by 
the Governing Council in paragraph 7 above, and encourages 
other organizations with expertise in this area to support the Iraqi 
Governing Council, if requested; 
12. Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council 
on his responsibilities under this resolution and the development 
and implementation of a time-table and programme under 
paragraph 7 above; 
13. Determines that the provision of security and stability is essential to 
the successful completion of t he political process as outlined in 
paragraph 7 above and to the ability of the United Nations to 
contribute effectively to that pr ocess and the implementation of 
resolution 1483 (2003), and authorizes a multinational force under 
unified command to take all necessary measures to contribute to 
the maintenance of security and st ability in Iraq, including for the 
purpose of ensuring necessary conditions for the implementation 
of the time-table and programme as  well as to contribute to the 
security of the United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq, the 
Governing Council of Iraq and other institutions of the Iraqi interim 
administration, and key humanitarian and economic infrastructure; 
14. Urges Member States to contribute assistance under this United 
Nations mandate, including military forces, to the multinational 
force referred to in paragraph 13 above;

of the multinational force referred to in paragraph 13 above not 
later than one year from the date of this resolution, and that in any 
case the mandate of the force shall expire upon the completion of 
the political process as describe d in paragraphs 4 through 7 and 
10 above, and expresses readiness to consider on that occasion

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
any future need for the continuatio n of the multinational force,

20. Appeals to Member States and the international financial

21. Urges Member States and international and regional 
organizations to support the Iraq reconstruction effort initiated at 
the 24 June 2003 United Nations Technical Consultations, 
including through substantial pledges at the 23-24 October 2003 
International Donors Conference in Madrid;

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
22. Calls upon Member States and concerned orgnization to help 
meet the needs of the Iraqi people by providing resources

Copy of Press Release by Government of India on Security Council 
Resolution 1511 on 
The Government of India welcomes the unanimous adoption of 
Security Council Resolution 1511 on Iraq on October 16, 2003, as a 
positive step towards the restoration of  sovereignty of Iraq to the Iraqi 
people. 
We have taken positive note of the re-affirmation in the resolution 
of the rights of the Iraqi people to determine their political future, and 
in this context the mandate to the Governing Council of Iraq to draw 
up a time table and programme by 15 December, 2003 for the drafting 
of a new constitution and holding of democratic elections under that 
constitution However, the resolution lacks specificity on the timing of 
transfer of soverignty. 
311 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
SCR 1511 envisages strengthening of the role of the UN in Iraq in 
areas of humanitarian assistance, economic reconstruction and in the 
political transition leading to establishment of representative 
government. 
We have taken note of the appeal in the resolution to UN 
members states to assist the Iraqi  people in their efforts in the 
reconstruction of Iraq. In this c ontext, we reiterate our readiness to 
contribute to the restoration of infrastructure, medical, health, 
education, communication and other civilian needs of the Iraqi people. 
We will therefore be participat ing in the International Donors 
Conference in Madrid later this month.

288. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: 
SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: SHRIMATI 
SAVITA SHARDA: DR. ABRAR AHMED: 
-   Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India proposed a dozen of steps to 
Pakistan to ease the tension between the two countries; 
(b) if so, the details of the proposals sent by Government to 
Government of Pakistan; 
(c) whether Government have received any response from the 
Government of Pakistan; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH): (a) and (b) In continuation of Prime 
Minister's initiative of April 18,  and as a part of the step-by-step 
approach to normalise relations with Pakistan, India, on 22 October

contacts between the two countries. The proposals included 
resumption of civil aviation links to be followed by resumption of the

313 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2003] 
cricket; permission to senior citizen (above 65) to cross at Wagah on

Guards authorities of the two countries; the non-arrest by either side of

provision of free medical treatment to a second lot of 20 Pakistani

delaying conditions to others.

responded positively to the Indi an proposals of 22nd October, and 
agreed to a number of measures. He also announced that Pakistan 
armed forces along the Line of Control (LoC) have been issued

Subsequently, the Director General Military Operations (DGMOs) of 
the two countries agreed to observ e cease fire on the International 
Border, LoC and Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL) in Jammu and

Review/updation of labour laws is a continuous process in order to bring 
them in tune with the prevailing situation and emerging needs of the 
economy.Taking into consideration the requirement of productivity, 
competitiveness and employment generation and to update the provisions

unorganised sector etc. The Ministry has held consultations and 
interactions with the workers' representatives, employers' organizations, 
experts professionals etc. The recommendations of the Commission were 
also discussed in the 38th Session of Indian Labour Conference held on 
28-29 September, 2002 and in a National Seminar on Unorganised Sector 
Workers held on 7-8 November, 2002, also in a Tripartite Committee 
meeting held on 18-19 February, 2003 and in the Consultative Committee 
Meetings of the Ministry of Labour held on 07-02-2003 and 30.04.2003.

Session of Indian Labour Conference held on 16-18 October, 2003. Such

Poverty alleviation schemes in the country 
*   324. Prof. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) what is the total percentage of people living below poverty line 
in the country; 
(b) the details of the schemes formulated and being implemented 
by the Government for alleviate poverty in the country; and 
(c) the steps being taken by Government in this respect? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI 
SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) The Planning Commission estimates 
poverty at national and state level from the large sample surveys on 
household consumer expenditure conducted by the National Sample 
Survey Organization (NSSO) at an interval of approximately five years. 
Based on the latest such survey conducted in 1999-2000 (NSSO 55 th 
Round), the percentage of people living below poverty line in the country 
is estimated to be 26.1% in 1999-2000. 
(b) and (c) Government has introduced a number of programmes/ 
schemes from time to time to improve the conditions of the people 
living below the poverty line. These are inter-alia as follows: 
Swaranjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)— The SGSY was 
launched in April, 1999 following the restructuring of the erstwhile 
Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) and its allied 
programmes along with Million Wells Scheme (MWS). The objective of 
the SGSY is to bring the assisted poor families (Swarozgaris) above the 
poverty line by organizing them into Self Help Groups (SHGs) through the 
process of social mobilization, their training and capacity building and 
provision of income generating assets through a mix of Bank credit and 
Government subsidy. 
Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)—This scheme 
announced by the Prime Minister on 15.8.2001 was launched in 
September 2001. The schemes of Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY) 
and Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) have been merged under this 
programme w.e.f. 1.4.2002. The primar y objective of the scheme is to 
provide additional wage employment in all rural areas and thereby 
provide food security and improve nutritional levels. The scondary 
352 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
objective is the creation of durable community, social and economic assets 
and infrastructural development in rural areas. The SGRY is open to all 
rural poor who are in need of wage employment and desire to do manuaf 
and unskilled work in and around the village/habitat. 
Rural Housing—Indira Awaas Yo jana (IAY)—The composite multi 
pronged strategy for housing has been operationalised w.e.f. 1999-2000. 
The Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY) is the major scheme for construction of 
houses to be given to the poor, free of cost. It has an additional component, 
namely, conversion of unserviceable kutcha houses to semi pucca houses. 
Swarna Jayanti Shahri Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)— SJSRY is a 
Poverty Alleviation Programme for the urban areas which seeks to 
provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed or under-
employed poor through encouraging the setting up of self-employment 
ventures or provision of wage employment.

for guarantee cover under the Credit Guarantee Scheme has been removed.

SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA (Karnataka): Sir, rape committed on 
a girl or woman is the most heinous, inhuman and beastly act which 
shatters the life of the victim, wh o suffers agony, shame and taunts of 
society at large throughout her life.  The rapists do not even spare the 
infant girls of a few months. Even incest rape cases are on the rise. As per

in 1988 were 15,151; in 1999, the figure was 15468; in 2000, it rose to

1999 were 402; in 2000, the figure was 363, and in 2001, this was 651. As 
per the Bureau, on an average, 4 cases of rape per day were committed 
against SC and ST women in 2001. These are reported cases, whereas 
much more cases must be unreported due to coercion, social fear and 
other reasons. Recently, rapists did not spare even a Swiss diplomat, 
which tarnished the image of the whole nation. Rapes are increasing, 
because laws are not deterrent and trial is very slow. Cross-examination 
of victim is done shamelessly and victim prefers to keep mum and rapist 
goes scot-free emboldened. 
Hence, I demand that the Government should bring forward a 
legislation to provide for deterrent punishment, to the rapists, which should 
not be less than capital punishment, and special courts be established 
throughout the country to try rape cases in camera and rape victims be 
rehabilitated suitably.

SHRI EDUARDO FALEIRO (Goa): Madam, the Indian Council of Historical 
Research was created by the Government of India in 1972 as an 
autonomous organisation under the Societies Registration Act. As per 
the ICHR Service Regulations 3 and 6, Chairman ICHR is both controlling 
as well as appointing authority with regard to the Member Secretary. The 
post of Member-Secretary fell vac ant on September 15, 2003 and the 
Chairman appointed by office memorandum dated September 26, 2003 
was the senior most officer among t he staff to officiate as Secretary. 
However, in blatant disregard to the autonomous status of the Council 
and in gross violation of rules and regulations, the Government on October 
6, 2003 appointed another ad hoc Member Secretary, without consulting 
the Chairman. By coincidence, or otherwise, this Government appointment 
followed criticism by the Chairman ICHR of some history textbooks brought 
out recently by NCERT. As a result of appointment of ad hoc Member 
Secretary made by the Government, the functioning of ICHR has come to 
a stand-still. Grants which were to be paid to the Council last September 
have not yet been released by the Government and the Council is unable 
to disburse the scholarships due to  thousands of scholars across the 
country and financial support due to a large number of national 
organisations of historians and other institutions. 
In this context, I urge upon the Government to cancel the appointment 
made by it of ad hoc Member Secretary and to take steps to appoint a 
regular Member Secretary of ICHR in  strict compliance with rules and 
regulations.

SHRI P.G. NARAYANAN (Tamil Nadu):- Madam Deputy Chairperson,

Madam, the multi-purpose Inter-State Irrigation Project over River 
Subarnarekha was conceived of in the sixties of the last century and the 
construction got initiated in 1967 with an assured assistance from the 
World Bank. The chief purpose of the Project was to provide irrigation 
facilities to the farmers of West Bengal, Orissa and erstwhile Southern 
Bihar, a part of which is now Jharkhand. The Project intended irrigation, 
flood-control and generation of hydel-power. The Chief Ministers of the 
three beneficiary States signed an agreement in early seventies of the last 
century. But inordinate delay awaited the Project, firstly, on issue of 
rehabilitation of tribals from the Project site to other places and, secondly, 
for rise in the cost of construction. Today, the Project looks like a dying 
concern. In 1993, the cost of the Project was estimated at Rs. 790 crores. 
In 2003, it stands at Rs. 1,755 crores. It is also calculated that to irrigate 
the arid-lands in Jharkhand from Subarnarekha Dam and to provide 
drinking water facilities to Jamshedpur, the Project would cost Rs. 2,870 
crores. When the Project was agreed upon nearly four decades ago, Orissa 
expected irrigation of 1,10,000 hect ares of land in Mayurbhanj and 
Balasore districts. West Bengal and Bihar also had their high expectations. 
But hopes have receded because of indefinite delay. I appeal to the 
Government of India to remove the clouds of uncertainty and assure the 
concerned States that the Project will be implemented without further 
delay since substantial investments have already been made over the last 
several years. Disputes among States, if any, can be resolved amicably 
since the Subarnarekha Project will benefit all the States. 
Problem of intelligent fuel adulteration in Delhi and other parts of 
India 
PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ (Jammu and Kashmir): Madam, I want to 
make a Special Mention on the devastatingly intelligent fuel adulteration 
business in Delhi and elsewhere. The crisis of fuel adulteration in India 
has, again, been highlighted by the Centre for Science and Environment. 
382 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
CSE has done a meticulous exercise to show that the intelligent fuel 
adulteration business seriously compromises improvements in vehicle 
technology, that are urgently needed to clean up air in our cities. 
Two years ago the Supreme Court asked the Environment Pollution 
(Prevention Control) Authority (EPCA) to conduct an independent 
investigation into the problem of fuel-adulteration in Delhi. CSE was 
selected by the EPCA to undertak e an independent study which was 
submitted to the Court in February, 2002. CSE has felt alarmed that 
even the Supreme Court's intervention has not made any difference to 
the magnitude and complexity of adulteration in fuel in India. This is 
primarly due to indifference of the administration in dealing with oil 
companies. CSE claims, rightly so, to have set out on the fuel 
adulteration trail and was shocked by the magnitude of adulteration. 
Almost anything, waste oil, surplus or pilfered solvents from industrial 
estates, even cheap imported kerosene are bunged into transport 
fuels. The CSE tracked this crime and witnessed rampant pilferage 
from oil tankers outside the Bijwasan oil terminal in Delhi, open sale of 
adulterated fuels from drums in garages, tea stalls and roadside 
workshops in Delhi and small towns like Meerut. 
The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas must take serious note of 
this menace, make the oil companies accountable, remove the laxity in quality 
standards of fuels, remove the gaps in the price of fuels, take regulatory measures 
such as tracking down the illegal use of naphtha and restore the penalties provided 
for this deadly crime. Thank You.

Plight of workers of textile industries in Tamil Nadu 
PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM (Tamil Nadu) : Madam, due to the poor 
monsoon this year, the textile industry in Tamil Nadu is facing a very 
serious problem and is in a very bad shape. The main reason being high 
price of yarn. Unfortunately, due to the poor monsoon, the growth of 
cotton has gone down drastically in the last two months. Nearly three 
lakh workers are dependent on the textile industry whose main source of 
income is yarn spinning, weaving and selling of finished textile products. 
Shortage of yarn has created an unprecedented situation of near 
starvation in the families which are involved in the textile industry. In the last 
two weeks, textile workers have staged agitations to ventilate their grievances 
in the major and important cotton-producing centres like Erode, Karur and 
Coimbatore. The main grievance of the textile workers is that they should 
be supplied yarn at a reasonable and affordable price. 
This is a very serious problem which may take the shape of a severe 
crisis, if not controlled and contained immediately by providing yarn at a 
reasonable price. Hence, I urge upon the Central Government to stop the 
export of up-country yarn immediatel y and come to the rescue of the 
starving textile workers of Tamil Nadu by supplying yarn to the weaving 
industry as they are adversely affected and also evolve a permanent 
solution to this problem which crops up whenever there is poor 
monsoon and indiscriminate export of yarn.

Shrimati Bimba Raikar to move a motion for consideration of the Women 
and Girls (Prevention of Stripping, Te asing, Molestation, Branding as

SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR (Karnata ka) : Respected Sir, I beg to 
move : 
'That the Bill to provide for the prevention and prohibition of stripping 
and parading the women or girls naked in public view, teasing, molestation, 
outraging modesty and branding and killing them as witches and offering 
as Devadasis and for deterrent punishment for such offences and making 
these offences as cognisable and non-bailable and for matters connected 
therewith, be taken into consideraiton." 
Sir, in most of the cities, the life of women has become unsafe. My Bill aims 
at curbing and eventually eradicating the most heinous and repressive crimes 
against women, mostly Dalits, in the name of the social customs and 
superstitions. Over many decades, we have been able to bring about social 
reforms for the betterment and advancement of the backward people and 
women. Many social reforms have sprearheaded compaigns against social 
evils like untouchability, sati, infanticide, devadasis, and killing and rape of women. 
Even now, despite advancement, both on social and economic fronts, Dalit 
women are still being treated and humiliated like bounded labour. Through this 
434 

[5 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
Bill, it is intended to ensure legislative support for eradicating such crimes 
against Dalit women as enumerated in this Bill. Also, I would like to say a few 
words about the devadasi system. Sir, the devadasi system is mostly prevailing 
in Kamataka, and in Andhra In devadasi system, the girl is offered in marriage 
in the name of God and after that, that girl is given to the main person in that 
place, say it is a Patel or somebody, on the first day. Then, that girl is treated as a 
prostitute. And what happens in small villages is that this leads to prostitution. 
And, what happens when people from Mumbai come to such places and give 
money to the parents. They attract the girls and these girls are taken to Mumbai 
and used as prostitutes. You must have heard about some red light areas in 
Mumbai. That is the place. After some time, when these girls come back to 
their villages with their fine saris, sandals, ornaments, cosmetics and other 
things, other girls also get attracted and feel like to go to Mumbai and these 
agents make money like anything. They give money to the poor parents who 
have no money. They take money and sell the girls and the girls are brought to 
Mumbai. Afterwards, for whole of the life, these girls become prostitutes. This is 
known as devdasi system. This is done in the name of God and such girls are 
just thrown out of the society. So, this system is really horrible. Even after 50 
years of our freedom, if the women are going to be treated like this, I think, it is a 
very heinous crime against them and a shameless thing. Whenever we read 
newspapers early morning, we find so many rape cases, killing of women, 
burning of women, women thrown out of houses. All these things are there in 
the newspapers. We read it everyday. But, what happens sometimes is that 
women do not get the help of police. Police are also such people that wherever 
they get little money, they get attracted, and they do not come to the light in 
some of the cases and these things take place. And, because of poverty, this 
type of injustice is done to women. Sir, I also feel that ours is a country where 
we respect women. We treat them as mother and as Goddess. Even when we 
take the name of any God, we never say Ram-Sita, we say Sita-Ram; we never 
say Narayan-Lakshmi, we say Lakshmi-Narayan. Whenever you send an invitation 
card, there you will first see Shrimati and then Shri. These things are there. We 
are known for our culture. We are not like women of other countries where there 
is no respect for marriage. Sir, to tell you one example, I have been to America 
where I was asked, 'What is this red thing you have put? For which, I replied, "It 
is the symbol of my marriage". They said, "What marriage and what symbol; we 
dont have anything like this". Somebody just asked me, "How many years of 
married life did you have'? I said, 40 years and new my husband is no more". 
Then I was asked, "How many husbands did you have in 40 years"? Then I

eplied, "we are Indians and we do not believe in a number of husbands. We 
stay with only one husband, if he is alive. And, even if he is dead, we stay like that 
only". They were surprised. This is what we are known for. We are known for our 
culture and for our goodness. But, when it is like this, when this type of injustice 
s done to women in our country, we feel very sorry. That is why, I decided to 
bring this Bill in this House and place it  for consideration of the hon. Members

they are not protected, they are not respected, their dignity and modesty 
are not preserved, how can we feel proud of our culture, our society or 
our own lives? Here comes the question of Government responsibility 
also. There is one single thing that the society must be aware of. The 
society must know how Jo behave. Every individual must be taught how to 
behave. If I do not behave properly, should there be no law to punish me, 
to deter me and to prevent me from doing something wrong? But what 
we find in our country today is that our women are not safe in our so-
called civilised society. We are proud of our culture. We are proud of our 
progress. We are proud of many other things. But we cannot be proud of 
ourselves as far as our etiquette and our behaviour Is concerned. So, this 
Bill is well-intentioned and well-intended.
